Age-specific death probabilities are rich but hard to grasp at a glance. Their time-dependent model packs the data into a few latent effects, with an autoregressive prior linking them across years. Bayesian sampling via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo drives the fit. On Human Mortality Database data for 41 countries, six latent effects rebuild the observed patterns well and beat a Gaussian factor model.
arxiv-2603-26575: Boeker and co-authors model how fear and muscle activity interact while people climb. Lead climbing allows longer falls than top rope style, which may change felt risk. The team records muscle, heart, and arm motion signals from 19 climbers in both styles. Climbers also rate their fear across climb phases. Mixed-effects and deep models with personal random effects track the link, and personal terms improve every error score. Muscle fatigue ties clearly to higher fear during lead climbing.
arxiv-2603-26675: Wan and co-authors present GeoBlock, a decoding method that sets block size in diffusion language models from attention geometry. Block diffusion refines many tokens at once, but safe block size depends on how tokens depend on each other. Fixed rules and local confidence hints miss that structure. GeoBlock reads cross-token dependency patterns to find stable regions for joint refinement. Tightly ordered zones get sequential updates, while cohesive zones refine in parallel. The method needs no extra training and plugs into existing block diffusion models.
arxiv-2603-26775: Lee, Lin, and Diao train a reinforcement learning agent to pick demonstration examples for visual in-context learning. The standard nearest-neighbour pick favours look-alike examples, which can repeat the same narrow slice of answers. Their agent builds the example set step by step to lift the main model's score. A dueling DQN with a query-focused decoder drives the choices across five visual regression benchmarks. Learned picking wins big on factual regression tasks, while nearest neighbours stay best for subjective preference tasks.
arxiv-2603-26875: Cerf and Ollivier introduce a perturbative method for studying quantum correlations. The set of quantum correlations collects all outcome statistics that separated parties can share. Their method uses Lie theory for the unitary group to track small changes in quantum strategies. Near classical points, a Bell operator splits into smaller blocks they call subset games. This shows the quantum set has a flat boundary near classical points. It also points to new proof routes for open problems on correlation sets.
arxiv-2603-27075: Osmond and Jego survey how regulators and industry define agentic AI, and find the definitions wrong on the tech. They compare eleven rulebooks and frameworks with six leading developer architectures. Legal texts conflate model capability with agentic architecture, the authors argue. They also credit token prediction with thinking. Autonomy appears as a simple scale, not a shift to looping, tool-using execution. The authors build a shared one from developer docs. Loose definitions, they warn, leave the real control points ungoverned.
arxiv-2603-27275: Azar and co-authors study frozen surface modes that appear when an emitter matches a wave's group velocity. Spatio-temporal modulation can mimic motion near light speed. Classic Cherenkov effects need phase velocity matching instead. When energy flow and emitter move together, the surface mode stands still in the emitter's frame. Resonant energy then piles up at that frozen mode. The local density of optical states jumps sharply as a result. Emitter power extraction and optomechanical forces grow with it. Slow surface modes make the regime reachable at modest speeds.
arxiv-2603-27375: Han and co-authors present KAWHI, a reward reweighting plug-in that ties visual evidence into RL for vision-language models. Verifiable-reward training boosts text reasoning but shortchanges the image itself. KAWHI first finds semantically salient regions by layered grouping. Attribution then finds the attention heads most critical for vision. Credit moves at paragraph level toward central reasoning steps. It slots into uniform reward methods like GRPO as-is. Diverse benchmarks showed gains from adding it.
arxiv-2603-27475: Agarwal and co-authors rebuild macroscopic quantum optics on first-order form. Standard theory uses second-order equations and drops boundary terms. Their approach keeps both electric and magnetic fields. Boundary terms stay in the math throughout. That choice yields a clean input-output framework. A Green operator moves the field state between surfaces. Symmetry gives reciprocity and an optical theorem with little fuss. Two noise sources appear: bulk loss and boundary fields. An exact commutator matches the fluctuation-dissipation rule.
arxiv-2603-28175: Mihm and five co-authors grow hematite thin films on lithium niobate, a piezoelectric crystal, by pulsed laser deposition. Hematite is a newfound altermagnet, a trait that suits it for spintronics. Films on y-cut substrates came out single-crystal, while z-cut films split into two domains turned 60 degrees apart. Both types show the temperature-driven spin reorientation that lets the Néel vector be steered. The pairing could serve future magnonic devices driven by sound waves.
arxiv-2603-28275: Jucha and Szczurek map out next steps for studying light-by-light scattering in ultraperipheral heavy ion collisions. Two photons from passing nuclei can scatter into two photons, a rare quantum effect. They discuss pushing to lower masses, where new mechanisms may appear, and using future detectors such as FOCAL and ALICE 3. They also propose inelastic cases where photons strike single nucleons, plus neutron-linked cross sections that could reveal them. Single-photon production gets its own estimates.
arxiv-2603-28975: Sommer and Winter reply once more in a long chain of comments on a claimed natural information measure. Their abstract calls the exchange tedious. They say that John Doe and Jean Roe have insisted on further comments on the authors' refutation. The authors feel compelled to review those views once again. They describe the opposing views as not even wrong. Their stated hope is to put some sense back into the discourse. The remark continues a nested sequence of comments, replies, and rebuttals named in the title.
arxiv-2603-29475: Seletkov and co-authors present Survival In-Context, a model for survival analysis on medical data. Survival tasks face small datasets, censoring, and mixed table columns. Their model is a prior-fitted network trained only on synthetic data. A generator framework builds varied survival datasets under a rich prior. The model learns to mimic Bayesian prediction under that prior. At use time, it predicts for each patient in one forward pass. No task-specific training or tuning is needed. It matched or beat classic and deep rivals.
arxiv-2603-29775: Conigli and co-authors update the hadron share in the running of the electroweak couplings. They give values for the electromagnetic coupling and the mixing angle up to 12 GeV squared. Lattice runs use five spacings and several pion masses, including the physical point. New kernel tools split short and long distance parts cleanly. That split sharpens precision over their past result. They compare with other lattice and data-based values.
arxiv-2603-29875: Tuora and co-authors argue that plain vector search nearly matches graph-based retrieval systems. Chunk vectors mix a chunk's facts into one blob and ignore links between chunks. Graph systems fix that but add huge indexing cost and heuristic search. Their UnWeaver splits documents into entities that recur across chunks. Retrieval then uses entities to recover the original text. On end-to-end QA, VectorRAG beats standard GraphRAG. It nearly matches top graph systems at a fraction of the cost.
arxiv-2603-29975: Liu and co-authors speed up FP64 work on GPUs by emulating it with INT8 math. Their SCILIB-Accel tool offloads matrix work in the LSMS materials code with no code changes. How well it works turns on both the math settings and the traits of the operator. Tunable settings let users dial the emulation to fit each case. Unlike mixed routes, the method keeps the original algorithms intact. It can lift speed and accuracy at once. The team backs such adaptive plans for future HPC.
arxiv-2604-00075: Saadat and Fellay benchmark two language models on curating functional evidence for genomic variants, using ClinGen annotations to test abstract screening and full-text evidence extraction. Both models catch most relevant studies, with recall between 88 and 90 percent, but the reasoning model o4-mini classifies full-text evidence far more cleanly, reaching 96 percent accuracy and specificity of 0.83 against 0.37 for gpt-4o-mini. The pair also assemble AcmGENTIC, an end-to-end pipeline that gathers literature, filters abstracts, extracts evidence, and drafts reports for human curators.
arxiv-2604-00275: Samer Abdulkarim and five colleagues test whether large language models can automate UML state machine generation from unstructured requirements, using specialized state machine designs. Two designs are tested: a structure-driven version making parts step by step, and an event-driven version letting found events guide building. Single-prompt drafts score 0.90 on states and 0.75 on transitions with Claude 3.5 Sonnet, but guards lag and actions fail for GPT-4o. A hybrid approach, fixing a single-prompt draft through a design, lifts GPT-4o to Claude's level without further raising Claude.
arxiv-2604-00375: Fang and colleagues examine a puzzle in diffusion language models. These models can in principle decode tokens in any order, opening richer paths through reasoning than autoregressive models allow. In practice, random-order decoding harms quality. Remasking low-confidence tokens improves single samples, yet it narrows exploration and limits multi-sample gains. The authors explain this quality-exploration dilemma in unified terms. They show remasking boosts a short-sighted quality proxy while provably shrinking the entropy of the output distribution.
arxiv-2604-00975: Sergey Ostapchenko takes up how model numbers for the muon content of wide air showers relate to traits of hadron-air events. Using a new Monte Carlo maker of cosmic-ray events, QGSb, he studies in detail how certain steps shape the muon number. He also covers constraints from lab data on those steps.
arxiv-2604-01075: Brumley and colleagues prove that joint eigenfunctions of all invariant differential operators delocalize on average for almost all symmetric spaces. The result covers any sequence of compact locally symmetric spaces that is uniformly discrete, holds a uniform spectral gap, and tends in the Benjamini-Schramm sense to the space. Delocalization holds when the spectral parameters sit inside a fixed spectral window.
arxiv-2604-01275: Benjamin, Fitzpatrick, Li and Thaler search for two-dimensional conformal field theories by turning modular invariance into a loss to minimize. They add an error gauge for cutting the spectrum short. They also use a new singular-value optimizer, Sven, that beats gradient descent on the layered landscape. The search yields candidate partition functions with central charges from 1 to 8 over 7, a range with no known examples, and points to a tighter gap limit near central charge 1.
arxiv-2604-01375: Aich and colleagues ask how good rubrics are, judging the scales used to grade AI agents with measurement signals. They introduce the RubrIc-Failure Taxonomy, nine ways a rubric can fail under reliability and validity. Each mode leaves a distinct signature. Seeding 720 corruptions into rubrics, a probe over the signals identifies the failure at 75.0 percent accuracy. That beats 56.7 percent for a frontier model asked to name the failure. In GDPval and Terminal-Bench, 10 of 48 expert rubrics weight criteria backwards, so a response can fail the key point and grade well.
arxiv-2604-01675: Nguyen and colleagues introduce frequency domain adaptation for appearance shifts in remote heart sensing. By transferring low-frequency parts encoding domain appearance traits, it helps models learn to ignore appearance shifts while keeping cardiac signals. They propose Harmonic-Constrained Optimal Transport, using cardiac signal harmonics to align original and FDA-transferred signals. Cross-dataset tests show the FDA and HOT method lifts strength and transfer of rPPG models across diverse sets.
arxiv-2604-01975: Barthelemy, Dusson, Hernandez and Zhang construct equivariant and permutation invariant function spaces without Clebsch Gordan coefficients. From a finite space stable under a connected linear Lie group, they use the Lie algebra to build a matrix whose kernel matches exactly the desired subspace. For key groups they pin down sparsity, rank and exact dimension, and show the method scales linearly with basis size rather than exponentially. Enforcing equivariance on top of invariance thus buys large savings when approximating such functions.
arxiv-2604-02175: Skrabulis and colleagues cancel shot to shot force noise in parametric squeezing tests. Slow stray forces stay fixed within one shot but shift between shots, spreading results and hiding quantum uncertainty. Their oscillator echo method, borrowed from spin echo work, cancels such noise fully in ideal tests. A demo with a levitated nanoparticle in light traps pushes noise down to the measurement backaction limit.
arxiv-2604-02375: Guerin and Guerin decouple agent execution from language model reasoning with KAIJU, an executive kernel for intent gated runs. ReAct agents suffer serial latency, quadratic context growth, and prompt injection and hallucination risks. KAIJU plans upfront, schedules tools in parallel with dependency aware inputs, and clears tools by scope, intent, impact and clearance. Three modes offer finer control for complex investigations. Against ReAct it lags on simple queries from planning overhead, matches at moderate complexity, and wins on parallel data gathering tasks.
arxiv-2604-02575: Sahoo and Pal build a decision scheme that helps power grids withstand wildfires amid variable renewable generation. Because dry, windy fire conditions are known a day ahead, their stochastic formulation combines day-ahead and real-time choices, coupling preventive and corrective actions with grid stability limits. Tests on a reduced 240-bus model of the US Western Interconnection show higher resilience across fire risk levels without losing economic viability.
arxiv-2604-02775: Umeh resolves a clash at the heart of cosmic matter clustering. The point-particle approximation, standard in clustering models, clashes with general relativity through spacetime singularities. He uses the fact that a matter horizon forms before caustics appear, letting singularities be isolated by spacetime surgery. Gluing distinct sheets across a shared boundary yields a backreaction term that matches gravitational edge modes. Those modes bend particle paths to give flat galaxy rotation curves with no dark matter particles. The framework offers a first-principles alternative to dark matter.
arxiv-2604-03075: Morris and Maes test whether learners care who they believe gives feedback, AI or human, in computing education. In a three-condition experiment with 148 participants, one language model's feedback is attributed to AI, instant or delayed, or to a human teaching assistant with the same delayed delivery. Believed human attribution lengthens time on task versus timed AI feedback, while delay raises output complexity. In the human-attributed condition, 46 percent disbelieve the attribution and fare worse than those receiving transparent AI feedback. Believed human presence may motivate, but only when credible.
arxiv-2604-03175: Caputo builds a new class of segregated solutions for coupled nonlinear Choquard equations in 4D. One part peaks as a radial ground state, while the other blows up at points forming a regular polygon. The proof uses a finite-dimensional reduction, linking rival systems to critical nonlocal problems while keeping known split patterns. The two parts keep apart.
arxiv-2604-03275: Kingston and colleagues present IPSL-AID, a diffusion tool that turns coarse global climate forecasts into regional detail. Trained on ERA5 reanalysis data, it makes temperature, wind, and rain fields at quarter-degree detail from coarse inputs and their space-time context. It also models fine-scale spreads for uncertainty, matching extremes, spectra, and spatial patterns well.
arxiv-2604-03375: Rogantini and colleagues study gas and dust toward the X-ray binary GX 340+0 using deep Chandra spectra. Fitting silicon, sulfur, and iron absorption edges together, they find amorphous olivine dominates the dust at about 65 percent, with metallic iron, iron sulfides, and fayalite behind it. They estimate about 74 percent of iron sits in silicates, showing iron is mostly locked in iron-rich silicate grains.
arxiv-2604-03475: Dai, Conejo, and Qiu propose a two-stage robust optimization plan that places power units early before severe weather hits, so load shedding stays low under the worst-case grid layout. The first stage schedules units in advance; the second dispatches power to cut load shedding under the worst-case grid shape. A problem-specific outer approximation method solves the model within a standard gap in reasonable time for mid-size cases.
arxiv-2604-03675: Erhan Zhang and colleagues built a training method for search agents that learn by trial and reward. Outcome-only rewards give thin guidance for middle search steps, and fixed judges grow stale as the agent improves. Their OASES system therefore scores each intermediate step by how well it supports the final answer. The judge and the search policy train together, and tests on five multi-step question benchmarks beat strong reinforcement-learning rivals.
arxiv-2604-03875: Chih-Tang Liao and colleagues revisited two squirmers, model microswimmers, swimming nose-to-tail in Newtonian and shear-thinning fluids. For the Newtonian case they derived an exact closed-form Stokes flow solution, cross-checked against finite-element simulations. The pair found co-swimming setups where both squirmers share identical velocities across a range of separations, explained by symmetry. Shear-thinning rheology reshaped propulsion, giving benchmarks for future many-swimmer studies in complex fluids.
arxiv-2604-04075: Fu Ma and team studied elliptic and triangular flow of light nuclei in lead-lead collisions at 5.36 TeV, using a coalescence model on MUSIC phase-space distributions. Simple nucleon-number scaling of v2 broke down at high transverse momentum, while an improved scaling held to higher momenta. v3 behaved similarly under both scalings, with no significant difference. Hypertriton flows proved insensitive to the Lambda-deuteron distance inside the hypertriton, matching early ALICE measurements.
arxiv-2604-04175: Qian Zhou, Yuanyun Zhang, and Shi Li proposed a framework for clinical foundation models that tracks uncertainty. Clinical notes are sparse, patchy, and mixed snapshots of a patient's true body state, yet most models pin each patient to one fixed point. Their model instead treats each patient as a spread over plausible hidden states, keeping views of the same patient in line. Across varied clinical tasks, it beat strong rivals on prediction, toughness under missing data, and well-tuned uncertainty scores.
arxiv-2604-04275: Garnavich and Fesen report weak, fast-moving sodium absorption in the spectrum of the stellar remnant at the centre of the supernova remnant from 1181 AD. The absorption sits near minus 61 kilometres per second, far slower than the remnant's expanding optical nebula at roughly 1000 kilometres per second. The authors briefly discuss what the feature might be and where it came from.
arxiv-2604-04575: Komaei Koma and colleagues probe unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models via compositional generation, focusing on nudity removal in Stable Diffusion. The team tests varied top unlearning methods with T2I-CompBench++ and GenEval plus set unlearning benchmarks. Results show a steady trade-off between unlearning power and compositional soundness. Strong erasure methods often harm attribute binding, spatial thought and counting, while shape-saving methods often fail at firm erasure. The findings show limits of current test habits and call for unlearning goals that save meaning beyond aimed suppression.
arxiv-2604-04775: Rafe and Das ask whether worry over driving safety in one's community pushes people to back AI driving. Using a Pew American Trends Panel sample, they fit a moderated mediation model with weighted equation methods and seven checks. Worry has a direct push toward rating AI driving above human driving, yet it also damps AI enthusiasm, which itself lifts AI driving ratings. The indirect path is negative at low, mean, and high driving frequency, so the two paths nearly cancel and the net total effect sits near zero.
arxiv-2604-04875: Li and six colleagues automate video mashups, recombining existing footage into smooth audio-visual pieces. The craft demands coordination across story, image, and sound. Their DIRECT system frames the task as satisfying multimodal coherence. It then splits work among three agents: a Screenwriter anchoring overall structure, a Director setting editing intent, and an Editor cutting shots with fine-grained optimization. They also release Mashup-Bench, a benchmark for visual continuity and auditory alignment, and report strong gains over leading systems.
arxiv-2604-04975: Hetman presents two Steiner systems S(2,7,505) and two Steiner systems S(2,7,589). A Steiner system of this form is a design in which every pair of points lies in exactly one block of seven points. The first case uses 505 points, and the second uses 589 points. Publishing these four systems resolves two of the 21 undecided cases for block designs with block length seven, as listed in the Handbook of Combinatorial Designs. The note is short and constructive, closing two open cases rather than developing a general theory.
arxiv-2604-05175: Uslu and three colleagues train a spread model policy to match expert spreads over shares in radio networks with noise. Steps from a method serve as draws from expert cases per network instance. Shares are treated as graph signals on channel graphs. The design is a U-Net stack of GNN blocks, tuned on channel and node states. At use it samples shares straight from spreads, skipping the expert policy. In control, time-sharing made shares hits sum-rate utility and minimum rates, with transfer.
arxiv-2604-05375: Guo and four colleagues tackle video analysis by multimodal language models on strained edge-cloud links, where running deep reasoning on every frame wastes bandwidth and slows alerts. Their DAT system lets a small edge model screen frames and wake the large model only for suspicious ones, then tunes transmission to meaning and bandwidth. Tests report 98.83 percent recognition accuracy with fully consistent outputs, plus much faster alerts under heavy congestion.
arxiv-2604-05575: Voria and five colleagues propose sensitive prompts, inputs that are not themselves biased but tend to draw biased or thin answers, as an early-warning lens for fairness. Their SensY dataset holds 12,801 prompts across seven themes, and hand review of 4,500 model replies finds frequent neglect of ethical and contextual stakes. A classifier predicting prompt sensitivity adds a preventive tool for developers.
arxiv-2604-05675: Helland trims a postulate-based path to quantum foundations, dropping the awkward claim of one hidden variable behind all open ones. From two maximal open variables, the complementary pair Bohr pictured, the full Hilbert-space formalism follows. The purely mathematical theory turns into quantum mechanics once the variables turn physical.
arxiv-2604-05775: Hou and five colleagues test language models on raw phage genomes with PhageBench, copying expert bioinformatics workflows. Across 5,600 samples in five tasks, thinking models beat chance baselines on contig spotting and host calls. Long-range thinking and fine-grained pinpointing stay weak, pointing to a need for sequence-savvy next-generation models.
arxiv-2604-06075: Pathak and three colleagues' 2026 paper presents a hardware-efficient quantum reservoir computing design for short-term load forecasting. The design uses a fixed, untrained quantum circuit with Chebyshev feature encoding and brickwork entanglement. It uses single- and two-qubit Pauli readouts and avoids quantum backpropagation. Tested on the Tetouan City Power Consumption dataset, the reservoir comes from a genetic search over 18 setups. Under 8-bit and 6-bit quantization, accuracy stays within 1 percent of the FP32 baseline. Readout memory falls by 75 percent for 8-bit and 81 percent for 6-bit, aiding edge use.
arxiv-2604-06875: Robinson and Yoshida extend Effpi with existential outside choice. Effpi writes strongly typed message-passing programs in Scala, with compiler checks that code matches protocol types and a plugin that checks deadlock-freedom and liveness via CCS encoding. The new branching step lets protocols move on based on the received message's label and take messages over more than one channel. A catch-timeout step handles missing messages with grace. Examples, including a Raft consensus build, show the added power.
arxiv-2604-06975: Wang and three colleagues detect contract atomicity violations with PSR², a static analysis framework. Rigid rules leave analyzers blind to context, causing high false rates on flaws from intermediate state inconsistencies. PSR² pairs a graph module finding suspicious sequences in flow graphs with a semantic module extracting dependencies and state facts from trees. A fusion module validates findings against an inconsistency model. On 1,600 samples it scores about 92 percent F1 in ERC-721 cases against about 52 percent for existing tools, and fusion nearly halves false positives.
arxiv-2604-08275: Piccirilli, Fraser, and Schulte im Walde analyze 297 verb-object pairs, like float idea versus suggest idea, in about 2 million sentences. Metaphor fills daily language, letting speakers express abstract ideas through concrete domains. While prior work studied metaphors cognitively, broad comparisons with literal language are few, especially for near-synonyms. With five NLP tools, the team extracts 2,293 features covering feelings, words, and syntax. They ask whether features differ between metaphorical and literal uses, and whether single verb-object pairs diverge internally.
arxiv-2604-08675: Cuozzo and five colleagues examine spin polarized magnetic adatoms decorating a square superconducting network, seeking topological superconductivity without spin orbit coupling. Localized Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states at adatom sites collectively form a weak topological phase, and tuning Fermi energy shifts the system to a bulk dissociated phase where edge bands separate from the bulk. Nodal lines and coexisting edge and corner modes appear, showing how geometry alone can control topological coupling.
arxiv-2604-08975: Patty and nine colleagues review polarimetry, the study of light's polarization, across planetary science and astronomy. Because scattering changes polarization, it shows things brightness alone hides, such as the makeup, grain size, shape, and porosity of surface dust. It also reveals the air around planets and even the faint polarized glow reflected by exoplanets. The review surveys recent advances in optical polarimetry and tools built in Switzerland under the PlanetS research network, and maps the wide science cases the technique can now address.
arxiv-2604-09075: Yang and three colleagues tackle benign instruction conflicts in large language models, which juggle orders from system, user, tool, and fetched sources. Prior work stresses hostile attacks but misses common, non-harmful conflicts in real settings. Their NSHA approach picks the fitting orders under ranked constraints through logic. At training time it distills solver-based choices into model weights using machine-built training. Tests on rules, task handling, tool use, and safety show gains under conflicts while keeping utility high in standard settings.
arxiv-2604-09175: Mayaki develops a theory of generalization and scaling for mixture-of-experts transformers. It separates active capacity from routing combinatorics, deriving a covering-number bound that scales with the active parameter budget plus a routing overhead. With standard risk analysis, this gives a generalization bound under a manifold data model, where approximation and estimation trade off as in dense networks. A constructive approximation theorem and derived scaling laws clarify what worst-case theory certifies and what must come from data or optimization.
arxiv-2604-09775: Mättig-Vásquez, Delgado, and Pereira present a quantum state tomography protocol for networked quantum computers that avoids assuming remote entanglement. The method extends least-squares tomography to multi-unit systems, using local steps and plain links between nodes. With entanglement within each unit trusted, it can run with unbiased bases. The team derives strict trace-norm error bounds for the method, with steep growth in node count, plus bounds for gauging negativity. Tests for systems of up to seven qubits across several devices back the bounds.
arxiv-2604-09875: Chiba and 50 co-authors outline the Subaru Prime Focus Spectrograph Galactic Archaeology survey, part of a 360-night Strategic Program. Nearly 2,400 fibers over 1.24 square degrees will gather spectra, with about 130 nights for Local Group galaxies. First, 18,000 member stars in six dwarf galaxies test whether dark-matter density profiles are cusps or cores. Second, 30,000 stars over 45 square degrees compare assembly histories of M31 and the Milky Way. Third, tens of thousands of Milky Way stars trace how its fragile outer parts responded to past accretion events.
arxiv-2604-10375: Alexander and Fabozzi split each risk contribution into two clear and distinct parts. One part tracks how shaky a single holding is when viewed on its own. The other part tracks how that holding moves with the rest of the fund. The lone part stays positive, while the joint part can raise or cut total risk. Two time series methods trace how both parts shift across changing market moods. The split keeps strict additivity and shows when a hedge truly offsets risk.
arxiv-2604-10575: Wang and six colleagues address a familiar trap in AI-assisted brainstorming. Language models hand users finished blocks of text that resist breaking apart, so people settle on early ideas too fast. Their NexusAI diagramming tool splits generated inspiration into typed functional fragments. Users can zoom between levels of abstraction and recombine fragments across dimensions to spark new directions. In a study with 14 participants, the tool improved design-space exploration, lowered mental effort, and helped users reframe problems.
arxiv-2604-10775: Picano and Schiro investigate how the weak-coupling Hubbard-Holstein model relaxes after a switch-on of electron-phonon interaction. A Migdal approximation covers electron-phonon coupling, with second-order perturbation theory for electron-electron interaction. Relaxation crosses over between electron-dominated and phonon-dominated regimes. Tracking the thermal buildup, they find a sharp propagating front in real time and mean-field iteration number. Electronic observables show the front even for weak quenches, but phonons only at stronger coupling. When both fronts resolve, they travel at the same speed.
arxiv-2604-10875: Jin and colleagues ask how standard design shapes results, through ASB 018, a standard for auditing probabilistic genotyping software used by United States courts for DNA samples. Weak standards can hide and lend trust to poor systems. Study of ASB 018 and five audit reports finds gaps between what the standard wants and what it allows. Passing audits need not set use limits from seen failures, though the standard aims at that. The authors trace the gaps to fuzzy wording and vague terms, ending with tips for writing standards and judging them.
arxiv-2604-11175: Wang and Liu hunt infrared glow around dead stars in DESI's early release. Combining survey photometry and fitting each star's energy distribution, they first flagged 72 candidates, then cleared blending and confusion to leave 62 reliable ones. The haul includes possible companion stars, brown dwarfs, and dust disks, many newly found, and pushes dusty white dwarf studies toward older cooling ages.
arxiv-2604-11475: Nasernejad and Toledo study the strong persistence index of ideals in commutative Noetherian rings, the smallest power from which colon powers stabilize. They also define fluctuation in colon powers, where the expected equality holds, fails, and holds again across increasing powers, or the reverse pattern. Both notions are studied for monomial ideals, with the paper's two aims being the index and the fluctuation phenomenon.
arxiv-2604-11575: Hu and four colleagues introduce MIXAR, the first generative pixel-based language model. Pretrained on eight major languages across Latin and CJK scripts and scaled to 0.5B parameters, it beats a tokenizer-based model on the same corpus for unseen low-resource languages, with the largest gains on the most distant scripts. MIXAR replaces adversarial training with a GRPO RL stage that rewards its own free-running generations, multiplying free-generation accuracy by up to 2.3x. It matches tokenizer-based models on test benchmarks and resists orthographic attacks better.
arxiv-2604-11775: Brioso and six colleagues make KernelSHAP explanations usable for patch-based CT scans in three dimensions. They limit the work to a chosen region and cache patch results, so unchanged patches are not recomputed. They test whole-organ units, regular supervoxels, and hybrid organ-aware supervoxels, and report computing savings from 15 to 30 percent. Regular supervoxels lead on perturbation tests, while organ-aware units read more clearly and flag false positives better.
arxiv-2604-11875: Debbrecht and thirteen colleagues track the sub-parsec jet of the active galaxy 3C 84 with multi-epoch, multi-frequency interferometry at 22 and 43 gigahertz. They follow how the spectral index gradient in the core region evolves. The goal is to test competing jet-launching models and to weigh the ambient medium and magnetic field layout. Across three epochs the spectra shift markedly, revealing dynamic filamentary structures, evolving fields, and complex interaction with surrounding gas, all shaping the innermost jet and possibly its high-energy emission.
arxiv-2604-11975: Hasan, Lee, Sarker, and Iqbal introduce M2HRI, a multi-mode multi-agent setup that treats each robot as an identity-bearing agent with personality and long-term memory, plus coordination guiding participation. Old multi-robot systems often treat robots as the same, missing how distinct identities shape user view and coordination needs. In a study with 105 people, most personality contrasts proved distinct and always shown. Long-term memory raised preference awareness and natural interaction, while contextualised coordination raised chat flow, response fit, and overlap avoidance.
arxiv-2604-12375: Amilcare Porporato and Lamberto Rondoni revisit a classic puzzle in dimensional analysis, the study of physical units. They show Boltzmann's constant links heat with mechanical motion. That link adds a size-based group to the usual dimensionless groups. In large systems the new group fades away, recovering the classic rule. Ordinary thermodynamics thus appears as the limiting case of statistical mechanics. It emerges when fluctuations shrink beside average values.
arxiv-2604-12575: Yinxi He and four colleagues generate varied images from a single source image. Single-image generation must capture the source's inner statistics without outside data. Older methods often lose structural layout, especially for large rigid objects. They also offer little control over placement of generated content. StructDiff adds an adaptive receptive field module to hold global and local patterns. Three-dimensional positional encoding then steers position, scale, and local detail. Tests show stronger structural consistency, visual quality, and spatial control. A language-model-based judging criterion is also proposed.
arxiv-2604-12975: Lin, Starykh, and Keselman study how spinons, split-off bits of spin, interact in a spin-1 chain where nearby spins couple through two rival terms. They show that a magnetic field or a single-ion anisotropy makes those interactions plain to see in dynamical spin and nematic correlations. Theory predictions are backed by matrix-product-state simulations of the microscopic model.
arxiv-2604-13075: Hasan and four colleagues build DeEscalWild, a benchmark for training small language models to de-escalate police-civilian encounters. Filtering 5,000 raw clips from public videos through human checks and model judging yields 1,500 high-fidelity scenarios with 285,887 dialogue turns. Small models fine-tuned on the data beat their base versions across automatic and human measures, and a tuned Qwen 2.5 model tops Gemini 2.5 Flash under equal conditions.
arxiv-2604-13275: Kukreja and seven colleagues state scaling laws for contextual entrainment, the habit of language models to favor tokens that appeared in context despite relevance. Across Cerebras-GPT and Pythia families, entrainment follows steady power laws with split trends by context type. Semantic contexts show decreasing entrainment with scale, while non-semantic contexts show increasing entrainment. The largest models resist false claims four times better than the smallest, yet copy random tokens twice as readily, showing scaling reshapes context sensitivity rather than fixing it.
arxiv-2604-13675: Morse and Kozsik survey obfuscation for Erlang programs at the source, syntax-tree, BEAM assembly, and bytecode levels. The goal is to thwart reverse engineering, decompilation, and recompilation while staying true to how the compiler, validator, loader, and virtual machine actually behave. They catalog opcode dependency tricks. They also cover receive-based loop encodings, irregular control flow, mutability-oriented slowdowns, and self-modifying code via dynamic module loading. Effective BEAM obfuscation, they argue, exploits gaps between high-level semantics and the lower-level model the toolchain accepts.
arxiv-2604-13875: Kriener and colleagues tune bilayer nickelate superconductors by pressing them hard and steering two knobs at once: band width and band filling. Tilting the nickel-oxygen octahedra pushes superconductivity to higher pressure, while added hole doping pulls it back. In the non-superconducting state they spot up to three odd features that may trace to density-wave order, despite impurity and oxygen-vacancy flaws.
arxiv-2604-14075: Şen, Hu, and Kuhn present multistage conditional compositional optimization for choices made when the future is unknown, joining multistage stochastic programming with conditional stochastic optimization. The method minimizes nested conditional means and nonlinear costs, with optimal stopping and dynamic risk problems as cases. Naive nested sampling hits the curse of dimensionality, with scenario counts growing fast as nests pile up. Their multilevel Monte Carlo tools grow only polynomially with accuracy. That means each stage waits for new facts before choosing, so early choices do not lock in later ones.
arxiv-2604-14275: Heckman, Hicks, and Murdia show that quantum field theory's non-invertible symmetries define quantum gates for a computation scheme with post-selection as a gate. Gate and geometric complexity extend to this setting. The authors supply distance measures that stretch Lie-group distance to continuous and discrete non-invertible symmetries and to linear mixes of unitary gates. Finding distances between non-invertible symmetries in 4D and 2D field theories, they show the simple objects of a symmetry class can be highly complex to compute.
arxiv-2604-14375: Kermiche proposes a modular design for sequential learning that walls each task off in its own expert module, curbing catastrophic forgetting. A distributed gatekeeper spots outliers to route new inputs, while teacher learning, student distillation, and router training run side by side during one local session, after which raw data is deleted. A tight-bottleneck autoencoder draws sharp borders in crowded latent space and flags returning tasks without spawning duplicate modules. Tests across vision and language tasks show strong retention with no loss of student fidelity.
arxiv-2604-14575: Lu, Wang, Zhang, and Zhang propose Generative Augmented Inference, treating AI outputs as features for human-outcome models rather than as direct proxies for true labels. Orthogonal moments give consistent estimates and valid inference under a flexible link between LLM outputs and human labels. Under random labeling, it is optimal among debiased estimators, better when AI outputs carry signal. In conjoint analysis, it halves error and cuts labeling needs by over 75 percent. In health insurance, it saves over 90 percent of labels while keeping decision accuracy.
arxiv-2604-14675: Connor and Fujimori build new cases of maximal surfaces in Lorentz-Minkowski three-space, the spacetime with one time direction. Their surfaces repeat in one direction and carry single cone-shaped singular points. They adapt the Weierstrass representation of doubly periodic minimal surfaces with parallel ends. The result is entire periodic graphs whose singular points take a cone-like form. A singular point marks a place where the surface stops being smooth.
arxiv-2604-14775: Elbar studies a 1D cross-diffusion system for two populations on a torus, with a linear pressure law and different mobilities, but no self-diffusion. Each group moves in response to the other group. For any bounded non-negative starting data, Elbar shows that every admissible scheme yields global weak solutions. The argument introduces admissible sequences and proves a subsequence of any such sequence converges to a weak solution. Entropy estimates and the div-curl lemma, framed with Young measures, carry the proof.
arxiv-2604-15475: Zhou and ten colleagues present NeuroMesh, a decentralized neural inference scheme that lets mixed robot teams share one run stack. It sets one pipeline for how robots encode sights, pass messages, merge data, and decode tasks. The pipeline joins two merging styles for reduction and broadcast fusion, with a design that frees cycle time from latency. Tests on mixed aerial and ground teams across seeing, control, and task assignment show steady work.
arxiv-2604-15975: Klein and Zejly study the double Schwarzschild solution for equal masses in bispherical coordinates, a setting for two black holes of the same mass. They give an explicit conformal transformation from cylindrical Weyl coordinates to this system in terms of elliptic functions. They also present a multi-domain spectral method in these coordinates, built to numerically rebuild the solution.
arxiv-2604-16275: Mehta, Saxena, Chhikara, and Kumar study politeness effects on large language models across languages and models, using the PLUM corpus. Drawing on politeness theory and an impoliteness framework, they test three languages, five models, and three interaction histories, with 22,500 prompt-response pairs judged on eight factors including coherence, clarity, depth, and toxicity. Tone, dialogue history, and language strongly shape performance. Polite prompts lift average quality by up to about 11 percent, impolite tones worsen it, but effects vary by language and model.
arxiv-2604-16375: Pramaa, Danforth and Dodds map where graduates of top schools move, using LinkedIn ad data for 1,504 ranked schools in 102 countries. Talent flows proved highly concentrated, with the United States taking the largest share and the United Arab Emirates emerging as a notable regional magnet. The overall gender gap was modest but swung sharply by destination, and job entry ran through business roles everywhere while technical specialisms clustered in innovation hubs. Economic strength, stable institutions and strong schools drove destination pull.
arxiv-2604-16475: Xu and colleagues build a large language model driven by spikes instead of dense matrix multiplication. Their SDLLM replaces dense products with sparse additions, using a two-step gamma-SQP spike encoding that keeps quantization aligned with meaning, plus bidirectional encoding under symmetric quantization and membrane clipping. Spike trains with few or no firings dominate, cutting firing rates and halving time steps. Compared with earlier spike-based language models, it cut inference costs and improved accuracy by about 4 percent, pointing toward event-driven neuromorphic chips.
arxiv-2604-16575: Lima and colleagues test time versus shape features for DDoS anomaly detection in 5G networks. Most studies fix one format without checking which feature space matches the data. Their framework chooses between the two before training, using self-link and PCA variance checks. When probes prove unclear, a hybrid option stays reserved as a future fallback, not a proven branch. On two datasets with three tools, shape features matched or beat time ones. The gap widened as time ties weakened.
arxiv-2604-16875: Leutenegger tests four learning rules in same networks against human fMRI using pattern match study. A fresh baseline splits the architecture's share, with models trained at 32 pixels and tested at 224 pixels. At V1 the untrained base exceeds backpropagation, zero point zero five three versus zero point zero two two, and the same holds at V2. That edge dies at the 32-pixel training resolution, showing it depends on evaluation scale. At LOC, BP, guess coding and plasticity exceed the base, while at IT no conditions can be told.
arxiv-2604-16975: Saleh gives the first error bounds for approximating functions with Hermite expansions composed with adaptive coordinate transformations. His equivalence principle links work in the transformed basis to work on the function's pullback in Hermite functions. A rising transport map that aligns a smooth decaying function with the Hermite basis then yields fast spectral convergence, and explains flow-based adaptive methods.
arxiv-2604-17175: Kshirsagar and seven colleagues present RosettaSearch, an inference-time tool for backbone-based sequence design. Large language models act as the tool inside a search algorithm balancing search and use, scored by RosettaFold3 on a fixed budget. Applied to 400 weak strings from LigandMPNN, it finds designs that single-pass decoding misses. Design scores improve by 18 to 68 percent, and success rate rises 2.5-fold over the baseline. Gains hold under an outside Chai-1 check, reach across two model families, and extend to ProteinMPNN designs on de novo backbones.
arxiv-2604-17675: Coll and Hylton find the adjoint cohomology of seaweed, or biparabolic, subalgebras, a large, rich class inside simple Lie algebras. If such a one cannot be split, its adjoint groups are all zero, making it fully rigid. If it splits, the Coll-Gerstenhaber split for Lie semidirect products gives each group through outer powers of the center's dual and the zero-weight cohomology of the quotient by the center. The center is the unique source of real groups, and never splitting is exactly the test for this stiffness.
arxiv-2604-17875: Zhao and thirty-four colleagues calibrate the Gamma-Ray Monitor aboard the SVOM satellite, focusing on atmospheric albedo, the reflected photons that distort its energy response. When the detector points away from Earth, albedo contributes at most about 10 percent of total effective area, near perpendicular incidence. When it does not point away and bursts arrive beyond about 90 degrees, albedo can dominate, reaching around 100 percent, notably at 8 to 20 kilo-electronvolts where direct area falls to zero. Ignoring it would bias spectra and positions.
arxiv-2604-17975: Jeon, Hyojoong Kim, Nakwoo Kim, Poole, and Ray place two-dimensional supersymmetric theories on spindle-shaped spaces. A spindle is a surface pinched at two points. Building from five-dimensional supergravity solutions, they cover both the twist and anti-twist ways of keeping supersymmetry. They then use localization to compute an exact partition function and give one formula covering both cases.
arxiv-2604-18175: Moiola, Galante, and Parolin propose a recipe for picking evanescent wave bases in Trefftz methods. Standard Trefftz methods build Helmholtz solutions from traveling plane waves but break down badly in practice. Waves that fade instead of traveling can ease that breakdown a lot. Tests with the Ultraweak Variational Formulation show much better results with this choice, and more details will come in a follow-up paper.
arxiv-2604-18475: Ranjan, Singh, Kumari, and Jamil study the prime-coprime graph of a finite group, joining elements whose orders share only 1 or a prime divisor. They characterize exactly which finite groups yield split graphs. A general lower bound covers the independence number for arbitrary finite groups. Explicit values follow for cyclic, dihedral, dicyclic, and semidihedral families, mapping independence across distinguished group types.
arxiv-2604-18675: Bucca and three colleagues derive a theory of fluctuating hydrodynamics for the SYK lattice, a local version of a model central to many-body quantum chaos. They start from the nonlinear action of pseudo-Goldstone bosons that dominate at low temperatures. In the long-wavelength limit, they recast that action as an effective theory of fluid-like fluctuations. They work out this effective action to high orders in the derivative expansion. They pin down matching transport coefficients, deriving fluid behavior from a microscopic account of a strongly coupled quantum system.
arxiv-2604-18775: Luo and Gowda study multi-sample auditing for jailbreak detection in large language models, using the JailbreakBench Behaviors data set and several generator models of varying alignment. They test a lexical TF-IDF detector and an inconsistency detector across sampling budgets. Judging one output alone understates vulnerability, since more sampled outputs reveal more harmful behavior. Gains are largest moving from one output to moderate sampling, with larger budgets giving diminishing returns, and signals transfer partly across models. Code will be released.
arxiv-2604-18975: Jian and six colleagues tackle coordination noise in open world multi agent Minecraft systems. Current methods treat any local anomaly as a trigger to communicate, interrupting local work and overusing public channels. They split private execution states from public coordination states. An event triggered memory keeps compact low noise local states, while a gated escalation rule weighs criticality, recovery cost, and task impact before communicating. Tests on construction tasks show better blueprint completion and execution chains, stronger self recovery, and fewer wasted escalations.
arxiv-2604-19075: Jeon and three colleagues ask what powers Hebe, a helium-II emitting clump near GN-z11 seen by JWST. Candidates are a cluster of metal free first stars and an accreting supermassive black hole inside Hebe. Simulations allow a few hundred thousand solar masses of first stars at Hebe's spot, matching observations. Black hole light modeling gives ionizing rates and line luminosities fitting observations less naturally. The authors confirm Hebe as a primordial object powered most plausibly by a massive first star cluster, at the standard formation limit.
arxiv-2604-19275: Giacomossi and colleagues analyze timing on a Raspberry Pi 5 running the PREEMPT_RT Linux kernel. They ask whether one general-purpose system can host both high-level autonomy and low-level drone flight control. They isolate how kernel activation paths affect a 250 Hz control loop under heavy stress. The standard kernel proves unsuitable, with worst-case delays above 9 ms. PREEMPT_RT cuts that figure by nearly 88 percent to under 225 microseconds, and hardware memory contention remains the main residual jitter.
arxiv-2604-19475: Sanabria, Varela, Rocha, and Cardozo present maude2athena, a tool translating Maude's equational theories into Athena for equational and inductive reasoning. In rewriting logic, such specs define fixed function conduct, abstract data types, and standard data forms, using signatures and equations read modulo basic axioms. It supports execution and symbolic reasoning, but offers no native support for proof by induction. The tool moves Maude theories into Athena, a theorem proving language for natural deduction proofs over many-sorted first-order logic specs.
arxiv-2604-19575: Ren and colleagues study quasiperiodic elliptic equations using a standard projection method. The first problem becomes a degenerate periodic variational problem on a higher torus. The main difficulty lies in the projected problem's flaw: the setup is coercive in projected Sobolev spaces from the matrix, but not for the standard Sobolev norm. The authors prove soundness and regularity bounds within those spaces, though such smoothness alone may yield very slow Fourier approach for standard spectral work.
arxiv-2604-19775: Padhi and 11 colleagues present a framework for interpreting how concepts evolve over time inside language model agents, using a step-wise conformal lens. The method combines step-wise reward modeling with conformal prediction to label each step's internal representation as good or failing. Linear probes then learn from those representations to find directions of concept change over time, revealing the hidden workings behind sequential agent behavior.
arxiv-2604-19875: Yücel and Achouri ask when a metasurface, a thin engineered sheet, can be truly invisible, passing light with no reflection and no phase lag. With the same medium on both sides, invisibility needs extra freedom, like angled light or higher-order responses. With different media above and below, a simple dipolar sheet needs magnetoelectric coupling. Anisotropic sheets can supply that coupling in effect, and simulations confirm invisibility at an air-dielectric interface.
arxiv-2604-19975: Carvalho and Hillenbrand weigh FU Orionis stars, young stars whose disks flare hugely during eruptive outbursts lasting decades. Outbursts lift disk brightness to about one hundred times the star itself, hiding the star while Keplerian rotation in the disk still betrays its mass. From high-resolution infrared spectra of several tens of FUors, they model line shapes and infer the mass distribution. That distribution matches the Solar neighborhood initial mass function, suggesting every young star passes through a FUor phase.
arxiv-2604-20575: Shastri proves that every fan-in 2 noncommutative arithmetic circuit computing the palindrome polynomial has size at least on the order of n times d. When d equals n, that gives a quadratic lower bound, on the order of n squared. The proof builds on and refines the author earlier work. Key proof ideas were generated by Gemini 3.1 Pro, a language model, which the paper discloses.
arxiv-2604-20675: Petiton, Grigis, Vock, and Duchesnay improve medical clarity of linear brain-scan models through feature whitening. Linked brain regions make weights reflect shared rather than own-region shares. They apply whitening to region groups with shared variance, plus a variant with tuned strength. They test region marks in two mental sorting tasks, telling bipolar illness or schizophrenia from healthy controls. Unlike PCA or ICA, which use whitening to reduce axes, their approach keeps the full input signal, suiting reading over choice. Whitening lifts weight clarity while keeping forecast scores.
arxiv-2604-20775: Wang, Nepote, Franzese, and Michiardi present a method for gauging the Kullback-Leibler divergence between chance laws on function space, yielding a tractable tool scalable to real snapshot data. They test their tool on a benchmark suite, where estimated functional KL nearly equals analytic KL. On synthetic and real scRNA-seq data, they show that current metrics often give mixed scores. Path-space KL enables a match-up of trajectory inference methods and exposes gaps in seen flows, where data is sparse or missing.
arxiv-2604-21175: Eleanor Wiesler and Trace Baxley speed up max-flow computation and image segmentation by letting a graph neural network rank edges for the classic Ford-Fulkerson method. Their message-passing network learns which edges likely belong to high-capacity cuts, and a priority queue steers augmenting-path search toward them. The scheme preserves max-flow optimality while cutting the number of augmentations, and theory links prediction quality to the speedup.
arxiv-2604-21375: Qijun Han and 13 colleagues build VLAA-GUI, a framework teaching GUI agents when to stop, recover, and search. A completeness verifier cross-examines finish claims against visible evidence, a loop breaker switches modes and forces strategy changes after failures, and an on-demand search agent looks up unfamiliar workflows. Coding and grounding agents join for code-heavy and precise actions. Across five backbones on Linux and Windows tasks it leads both benchmarks, scoring 77.5 percent on OSWorld and 61 percent on WindowsAgentArena, with three backbones beating human OSWorld performance.
arxiv-2604-21475: Xiangyu Ren and six colleagues suppress fusion erasure errors in photonic measure-based work, where graph-state building hinges on chance fusion operations. Prior compiler OneAdapt handles fusion failures but ignores erasures from photon loss, which can damage far more. Their tree-encoded fusion scheme, built on spin-qubit quantum memory, suppresses erasures during graph-state building, inside a tool system with methods cutting run overhead. On six benchmarks across program scales it beats other fusion encodings in robustness and improves vastly over OneAdapt, with feasibility shown on real hardware.
arxiv-2604-21975: Orlowski-Scherer and seven colleagues report a glue joint in a strut for the Simons Observatory telescope receiver. Stiff, cryogenically insulating struts keep detectors at temperatures and locations. A tapped hole and set screw profile the joint's walls, changing failure mode from adhesive to cohesive. The joint's yield strength is 10 percent higher than a smooth-walled design, and ultimate strength 33 percent higher. Measured yield versus predicted load gives a factor of safety of 7. The struts served three years with cycles from 300 kelvin to 100 millikelvin and no damage.
arxiv-2604-22675: Quaresmini, Piccinin, and Breschi propose a plan for epistemic injustice in algorithms. Algorithms are epistemic setups ruling access and social belief. Mainstream audits gauge fairness by error rates, calibration, or parity, leaving epistemic harms thin on theory and thin on counts. They bring in a deficit model showing injustices as gaps between ideal and real conditions across credibility, uptake, and agency. Mapping deficits to mediation stages shows epistemic injustice can last even when fairness constraints are met. Using fairness indices, they split resource inequality from a capability stance.
arxiv-2604-22875: Collins and five colleagues present SketchVLM, a training-free framework letting vision-language models annotate images with editable SVG overlays to explain answers, instead of text alone. Humans point and draw when explaining image reasoning, while text-only answers are hard to verify. Across seven benchmarks spanning reasoning and drawing tasks, SketchVLM lifts reasoning accuracy by up to 28.5 percentage points and improves annotation quality over image-editing and fine-tuned baselines. Single-turn generation already performs strongly, and multi-turn generation opens further room for human-AI collaboration.
arxiv-2604-22975: Meunier and thirty-eight colleagues analyze the Perseus cluster atmosphere with XRISM Resolve observations. Average temperature rises from 3.3 keV near the nucleus of NGC 1275 to 8 keV at 10 arcminutes, matching Chandra and XMM measurements. Beyond about 60 kpc a single-temperature plasma suffices, but inside that radius the team finds more than one gas phase. A cooler component, spotted through wide wings on strong emission lines, moves faster and more turbulently than the hotter gas. It may link to merging halos or cooling gas disturbed by radio jets and lobes.
arxiv-2604-23175: Xu and Lin build a GPU-native framework for multi-area power grid state estimation, splitting the network into areas and keeping work on device. Fixed-sparsity templates score residuals and derivatives, and a fused kernel assembles local normal-equation blocks without forming explicit Jacobians. Each area is factored on the GPU in Schur mode, exporting a dense boundary block that feeds a smaller global boundary system solved on device. Tests on PEGASE 2869-bus, PEGASE 9241-bus, and ACTIVSg10k systems show the design exploiting GPU throughput through full device residency.
arxiv-2604-23275: Yang and Yang link rogue-wave and lump patterns to root patterns of Umemura polynomials from the third Painlevé equation. In many integrable equations, when internal parameters grow large, rogue patterns follow the polynomial's roots. Each simple root yields a fundamental wave tied to that root, while a multiple root yields a non-fundamental wave near the origin. The same root rule predicts lump patterns in higher-order Kadomtsev-Petviashvili-I solutions at fixed time. A new transform turns bilinear Schrödinger rogue-wave solutions into higher-order KPI lumps.
arxiv-2604-23375: Hamlomo and seven colleagues compress image-classifying neural networks by grouping spatial regions and channels that activate together, then trimming each group with an adaptive low-rank split. Tested on a brain-tumour MRI classifier, the method cuts computing sharply while slightly raising accuracy, beating two standard compression baselines. The team reports settings that trade compression against accuracy along an efficient frontier.
arxiv-2604-23475: Cherilyn and Safaai map which channels in a language model's feed-forward layers matter most for its loss, using a Fisher-style sensitivity measure. They find a tiny core of loss-critical channels, dubbed supernodes, plus a weaker halo of channels sharing their wiring, and show the pattern holds across several model families. Pruning methods that protect the core keep perplexity far lower than baselines that cut into it.
arxiv-2604-23775: Li and eight colleagues survey safety for vision-language-action models, the shared base for embodied AI. Failures here can cause real physical harm. They sort threats and safeguards by attack timing and defence timing. This covers train-time poisoning and backdoors plus run-time patches, cross-modal tricks, jailbreaks, and freezing attacks. The survey also reviews benchmarks, six deployment domains, and open problems such as proven safety for embodied paths.
arxiv-2604-23975: Hashimoto and four colleagues simulate a market where traders with different risk tastes, patience, and information learn strategies by interacting. Instead of fixed trait-based rules, the traders take on distinct roles, and their dealings yield realistic fat-tailed price swings and clustered volatility. The work presents this joint design of learning and varied tastes as a working model of markets that organize themselves through adaptation.
arxiv-2604-24275: Chakraborty and four colleagues construct maximum matchings in general graphs in catalytic logspace, extending bipartite results. Building on Geelen's linear-algebraic algorithm, they first determine maximum matching size in catalytic logspace, then find a maximum matching in catalytic logspace with polynomial time. Using a similar Geelen algorithm, they solve the maximum rank completion problem in the same class, equivalent to linear matroid intersection. A PTAS for Edmond's problem yields a catalytic logspace algorithm approximating rank within any factor below one, giving bounds for maximum independent matching in linear matroid matching.
arxiv-2604-24375: Van Loock, Ahmed-Braun, and Tempere show that quantum droplets in a two-condensate mixture can lower free energy by splitting. Three-dimensional droplets split when interspecies interaction far exceeds intraspecies interaction and atom counts near the minimum for a droplet. One-dimensional droplets fragment when interspecies and intraspecies strengths stay close and density stays low for scattering length. As temperature rises, one-dimensional droplets split by expelling atoms, forming a gas of free atoms and pairs. Those pairs persist well above the transition temperature, informing droplet stability.
arxiv-2604-24575: Wang and colleagues turn a pretrained image-diffusion model into a general segmentation tool called DiGSeg. The method encodes the image and its mask together as conditioning for the diffusion network, while a text pathway aligned with CLIP injects language features at several scales. The result is a single system that produces masks from appearance plus arbitrary text prompts, with strong results on standard benchmarks and transfer to medical, remote-sensing and farming images.
arxiv-2604-24875: Behera, Schlafly, Meisner and Napolitano present a multiband version of crowdsource imaging. It fits multiple imaging bands at once in crowded fields. Images of the same sky region share the same sources at the same locations. Only fluxes vary between images. The framework also uses all images of a region to detect faint sources. Bandpass weighting is configurable. Similar concepts exist in DAOPHOT and DOLPHOT. Demonstrated on WISE W1 and W2 imaging, the multiband algorithm improves flux consistency. It reduces band-to-band position scatter over single-band fitting.
arxiv-2604-24975: Jue studies poisoning attacks on ALEX, a dynamic learned index that models the distribution of keys. He presents a unified, reproducible study of both attack types on ALEX. Evaluation handles realistic workloads with up to 200,000 adversarial inserts, across multiple datasets and a real-key baseline. Static poisoning barely affects lookup performance under bulk-loaded settings. Dynamic complexity attacks, by contrast, slow lookup throughput by up to 2.8 times. Attack success varies strongly by dataset, since dense keys limit adversarial leverage.
arxiv-2604-25175: Wei and seven colleagues develop a framework for multiplayer indirect reciprocity. Pairwise reciprocity is well understood, but collective action judges people against group reputation. They show stable group cooperation follows one rule: all good, help; one bad, halt. The rule is both necessary and sufficient, and it recovers the classical leading eight norms in the pairwise limit. Multiplayer systems, unlike pairwise models, show bistability and hysteresis around a tipping point. Tests find large language models shifting toward punitive defection with richer social information, yet missing the rule's logic.
arxiv-2604-25275: Nguyen and Safro present a meta-optimizer for QAOA generating parameter trajectories, giving strong starts in a few steps. Prior Long Short-Term Memory networks copying QAOA trajectories collapse to nearly one path. The optimizer uses graph embeddings and feedback from the QAOA objective, avoiding ground-truth angles. Evaluation covers MaxCut, Maximum Independent Set, Maximum Clique, Minimum Vertex Cover. Across 64 settings, the learned optimizer cuts optimization effort, improves results over standard starts, and transfers across graph families.
arxiv-2604-25375: Rouaida and two colleagues probe resonance spread in linked Duffing oscillators with fractional damping, a driver and receiver joined by a plain spring. Results split two kinds: spread resonance, where power balance fits direct transfer, and storage-led resonance, where the receiver still swings while power turns negative. Here, fractional memory helps store and release power with no push back on the driver. Tuning the receiver pitch off its match boosts the mix of low- and high-pitch replies, giving a mixed regime. Fractional memory can thus tune spread.
arxiv-2604-25475: Karan and three colleagues solve polarization-preserving wavefront rotation. A K-mirror rotates a wavefront but always changes transmitted polarization. Past efforts cut the change greatly, but need a tiny base angle or custom-index mirrors, and full independence stayed open. Half-wave plates before and after a K-mirror, rotated at half its angle, make transmitted polarization exactly independent of rotation angle. This works for any rotator, angle, index, and input state. They test a 30-degree base angle, finding mean error near 1 percent, limited by retardance flaws in plates.
arxiv-2604-25575: Yilmaz and three colleagues fluorinate bulk single crystals of La2NiO4 topochemically, a route to metastable phases that standard synthesis cannot reach. Past work used powders and films, so the team grows float-zone crystals and tries PTFE, PVDF, and CuF2 agents. They test direct and indirect contact paths to pin down how fluorine enters and spreads. Diffraction shows the frame survives while lattice spacings shift, and a new superstructure appears. Magnetic tests show a change in antiferromagnetic order after fluorination.
arxiv-2604-25675: Buralli and fifteen colleagues test how a segmented deformable mirror affects contrast on the HiCAT bench, a laboratory setup for imaging exoplanets with future large space telescopes. Small drifts can nudge the mirror segments out of alignment. That harms the faint images made with coronagraphs, which block starlight. Their lab measurements find aberrations below a nanometer, and simulations with injected segment errors degrade contrast to about two and a half times its starting level. The authors argue that sensing and controlling segment alignment will matter for the Habitable Worlds Observatory.
arxiv-2604-25775: Gu and seven colleagues introduce two convolutional backflow designs that push the efficiency-accuracy frontier for neural quantum states on strongly correlated lattice fermions. The Sparse Convolutional Ansatz for Lattice Electrons favors efficiency. It cuts backflow scaling from fourth to third power and speeds tests by more than forty times. The Accurate Convolutional Ansatz favors accuracy, setting a new benchmark on Hubbard and t-J systems. On the one-eighth-doped Hubbard model up to 32 by 32, the work finds no significant gap between horizontal and vertical stripe states.
arxiv-2604-25875: Hsiao, Cai, and Wang show that singly Cabibbo-suppressed D decays to a pion and an a0 meson open a new probe of CP violation. Measured branching ratios deviate sharply from short-distance expectations, pointing to long-distance rescattering. A D to K-star K to a0 pion path yields an amplitude comparable to the direct one, with strong phases essential for CP violation. Direct CP asymmetries then arise at the level of one thousandth, all negative in the reported channels.
arxiv-2604-26175: Azfar and four colleagues develop a hardware-grounded hybrid quantum optimization framework for transport problems such as vehicle routing, sales tours, and facility location. Approximate quantum compilation compresses early segments of digitized adiabatic steps into shallow circuits. With variational layers, it shows how start, depth, and expressivity interact on near-term hardware. Run on an IBM gate-based machine, moderate compression cuts two-qubit gate depth while keeping feasible-solution discovery steady or better for routing. Gains depend on fit between the compressed prefix and the variational ansatz.
arxiv-2604-26275: Bhati surveyed how agentic AI is reshaping software engineering, moving from tools that finish single lines to systems that handle whole repositories, features, or algorithms. The paper lays out a six-layer reference design and contrasts the classic lifecycle with an emerging agentic one. It also gathers evidence on performance, productivity, and jobs. Benchmark scores climbed from under 2 percent to over 78 percent, while about half of sampled jobs in 2026 used AI for at least a quarter of tasks.
arxiv-2604-26775: Fructuoso-Bonet and Rodríguez-López generalize aggregation functions, tools that combine many values into one, to maps between quantales, algebraic structures used in logic and order theory. They show these functions are exactly the lax morphisms of quantales, giving one shared framework for studying aggregation. From that framework they recover known results about combining metrics and fuzzy metrics, measures of distance with graded truth. The paper thus unifies scattered aggregation results under a single theory.
arxiv-2604-26875: Maybee and seven colleagues compare three year-long global km-scale runs of East Atlantic seed vortices, the swirls that can grow into hurricanes. Tracking seeds, easterly waves, cyclones, and storm systems against past data and satellite views, they find the explicit-convection run makes fewer, weaker hurricanes. Its seeds fail to keep strong upward mass flux offshore, a flaw tied to small storm anvils and stratiform rain. Runs with parameterised convection boost seeds more at the West African coast and form more hurricanes offshore.
arxiv-2604-27075: Fu and five colleagues present PhantomRun, a unified layer and dataset for retrieval, storage, and reproduction of CI build logs and metadata. Embedded builds often fail from cross-compilation, board setups, and toolchain limits, while logs vanish quickly and resist reuse across varied runners and formats. Across 4628 failing runs, PhantomRun rebuilt 91.8 percent of builds and kept outcomes in 98 percent of cases. Rebuilt builds match originals closely, differing only in timestamps or minor reordering.
arxiv-2604-27475: Peng and Wang study how spectral truncations of compact quantum groups converge in the Gromov-Hausdorff sense. Using a proper length function, they build a Dirac operator and its spectral truncations. Their result extends earlier convergence work on tori to a broad class of quantum groups, covering both compact and discrete cases. The work applies to groups such as SU(N) and SO(N), and to discrete quantum groups with rapid decay.
arxiv-2604-27675: Noronha, Kaneko, and Fujimoto develop a minimal nonlinear model for delay-driven oscillations in plant roots. Roots sense gravity and correct growth toward the vertical, and evidence points to a delay in this gravitropic correction. Their model predicts whether a root oscillates or grows straight down and finds a fourfold relation between delay and period, robust across response functions. Images of Arabidopsis show the oscillatory arc length mode is similar for inclined and vertical growth, and measured lengths match the model, supporting the fourfold delay-period rule.
arxiv-2604-27875: Zhou and six colleagues hunt fake pictures with a net joining scene meaning to fine ripple clues. They blame two faults: a lean toward marks tied to one maker, and a clash between high-level meaning and low-level ripple patterns. Their FGINet masks ripple bands to widen trusted clues, then feeds gated ripple cues step by step into the vision backbone. A compactness rule with a cosine margin pulls same-kind shots tight and apart from other kinds, and tests show top scores that carry to new sets.
arxiv-2604-28075: Aynetdinov, Haller and Akbik ask whether German language models should train once on diverse web data or repeatedly on a strictly filtered high-quality core. Filtering hundreds of millions of web documents and comparing both regimes across model sizes, they find repeated high-quality data wins consistently, even after seven epochs. Their released Boldt models reach state-of-the-art results while training on far fewer tokens than comparable systems.
arxiv-2604-28175: Zhao and Georgantas present Strait, a serving system for machine learning inference that protects deadlines for dual-priority traffic under heavy GPU load. It models contention during data transfer and kernel interference with an adaptive predictor, then schedules by priority from those predictions. Under intense workloads it cuts deadline misses for high-priority tasks by a notable margin at acceptable cost to low-priority work, and treats tasks more equitably than software preemption approaches.
arxiv-2605-00875:
Dustin M. Haggett systematically compares visual encodings of price charts for predicting cryptocurrency market regimes. Traders have long read candlestick charts by eye, yet deep learning on financial chart images remains little studied. Haggett tests three image encodings, five chart component choices, four network architectures, and ImageNet transfer learning in eight controlled experiments on Bitcoin, Ethereum, and stock index data from 2018 to 2024.

A simple four-layer convolutional network on raw candlestick charts performed best, beating larger pretrained models. Simpler choices, such as price-only charts at modest resolution, consistently beat more complex alternatives. GradCAM analysis aids interpretation, and transfer learning still improved results by a clear margin despite the gap between natural images and financial charts.
arxiv-2605-00975:
Tom Williams and two co-authors introduce a preparation version of contextuality within the sheaf-theoretic framework. Measurement contextuality arises when local measurement data cannot be fitted to one global picture. The new case is dual: locally set preparation data may fail to extend to a single global response matrix that fits all source contexts. That failure witnesses contextuality.

Unlike marginalisation for measurements, extending partial conditioning data is by nature non-unique. The authors therefore identify minimal structural and matching conditions for admissible extension matrices. Those rules force a rigid product form. That matching then marks the cases where the obstruction is truly nontrivial. A quantum example illustrates a system that exhibits this form.
arxiv-2605-01075:
Johannes B. Thalhammer and thirteen co-authors introduce Neighbor2Inverse, a self-supervised denoising method for low-dose phase-contrast CT imaging of the lung. Phase-contrast imaging gives high contrast for lung structures, but clinical use needs substantial dose reduction, which adds noise. Supervised denoising needs paired low and high dose data that are rarely available, and most self-supervised methods fit the phase-contrast reconstruction problem poorly.

Each noisy projection is split into two variants that keep structure but carry independent noise, following the Neighbor2Neighbor principle. Separate reconstructions form training pairs for a denoiser in the image domain. In region-of-interest experiments the method beats analytical and self-supervised baselines on noise suppression while keeping fine detail, and it also performs competitively on clinical CT data.
arxiv-2605-01275:
Suyoung Choi studies small covers, a family of four-dimensional spaces built from simple flat shapes. Choi asks which of them can carry a symplectic structure, a kind of paired geometry used in physics and pure math. The work sits in topology, the study of shape that ignores stretching.
